solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Catamaran at sea carrying key historical document

indicators.note: carrying means holding another piece within it
at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of catamaran are jumbled

parts.note: G is a musical key

explanation.surface: A catamaran out on the water carries an important old paper aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange CATAMARAN ('at sea') to MANACARTA, then 'carrying' puts G, a musical key, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magna Carta is the charter King John sealed in 1215, a famous document from English history.

clue.text: Low temperature up in the air

parts.note: to low is to make the sound a cow makes, moo

explanation.surface: A weather report: a cold reading high in the atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective for the temperature but is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A moot point is one still open to debate, unsettled, just as an undecided question is up in the air.

clue.text: Recovered from attempt to upset clergyman

parts.note: a go is an attempt or try

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so in this down clue the word is turned upside down and read in reverse

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman's title

explanation.surface: Someone bounced back after trying to annoy a vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like it means annoy, but it flips REV over to VER.
explanation.definitionFit: To get over an illness or setback is to recover from it; the phrase is a past-tense idiom matching 'recovered from'.

clue.text: Hands are moved thus to adjust for fall

definitions.text: Hands are moved thus to adjust for fall

parts.words: Hands are moved thus to adjust for fall
parts.note: when clocks go back an hour in autumn (fall), one way is to turn the hands the opposite way to their usual direction

explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' reads as a tumble, but it is the American word for autumn, when the clocks go back an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning the hands of a clock backwards means rotating them counter to their normal direction of travel.

clue.text: A New York house former president put together haphazardly

parts.note: W is George W. Bush, the 43rd US president, known by his middle initial

explanation.surface: A New York home that a past president threw together carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put together' simply strings the pieces in order; W is the nickname of George W. Bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something anyhow means doing it carelessly, without order or method, so it is a synonym of haphazardly.

clue.text: Trains frantically, like top Russian women

indicators.note: frantically means in a wild disordered way, so the letters of trains are scrambled

parts.note: as means like, in a comparison

explanation.surface: Imperial Russian ladies train with frantic energy.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAINS rearranged ('frantically') gives TSARIN, and AS for 'like' completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsarinas were empresses, wives of the tsars, so they were the highest-ranking women in imperial Russia.

clue.text: It slows down horses when oats get cut by 50%

indicators.note: cut by half means each of the two words keeps only its front half, the first two of its four letters

explanation.surface: A rider calms horses by halving their feed of oats.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'when' and 'oats' are 'cut by 50%': WH and OA survive.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoa is the command a rider or driver calls to make a horse stop or slow its pace.

clue.text: Shelter in part of garden attached to hospital

indicators.note: attached to here means the hospital letter is joined on above the garden feature in this down clue

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
an arbour is a shady bower or alcove in a garden

explanation.surface: A sheltered spot in a garden next to the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attached to' sets the hospital's H on top of ARBOUR in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour someone is to shelter them, and a harbour is also a refuge for ships, a place of safety.

clue.text: Chap's projection president with computer company got

parts.note: John Adams and John Quincy Adams were both US presidents
Apple is the computer maker

explanation.surface: A president teams up with a tech firm for some project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'projection' sounds like a plan or forecast, but it is a bump on a man's throat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adam's apple is the visible lump of cartilage in the throat, most prominent in men.

clue.text: Last longer than guy dismissed first

indicators.note: first puts the word for dismissed at the front, ahead of the guy rope

parts.note: a batter who is dismissed is out, in cricket or baseball
a stay is a guy, a rope or wire bracing a mast

explanation.surface: A man outlasts others after someone is sent away first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' looks like a man, but it is a rope bracing a mast or tent, also called a stay.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstay is to remain longer than someone else, as in outstaying one's welcome.

clue.text: Courts imprisoning you and me in part of Europe

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding something locked inside

parts.note: atria are open central courts in Roman houses, plural of atrium
us means you and me

explanation.surface: Law courts locking up the two of us somewhere on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courts' reads as law courts but means courtyards, ATRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a country in central Europe, so it is one region of the continent.

clue.text: Spy organization about to infiltrate cult ceremony

indicators.note: to infiltrate means to get inside, so about goes within the cult

parts.note: a sect is a religious cult
re means about, concerning
a service is a religious ceremony

explanation.surface: An agency of spies plants an agent inside a cult's rituals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a link meaning concerning the cult, but it supplies RE, the short Latin-derived 'regarding'.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret service is a government intelligence agency, the body that runs spies.

clue.text: Reward to soldier is burden on state

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the burden comes after the state

parts.note: Victoria is a state of Australia
a cross to bear is a burden

explanation.surface: A soldier's prize is a weight placed on the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like the nation, but it is the Australian state of Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria Cross is the highest British military decoration for gallantry, awarded to servicemen.

clue.text: Colleague in final chess position taking bishop

indicators.note: taking means taking in, holding the bishop inside

parts.note: stalemate is a final drawn chess position where a player cannot move
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A chess game ends with a bishop being captured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' sounds like a chess capture but signals B going inside STALEMATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stablemate is a horse from the same stable, and figuratively someone from the same organisation, a colleague.

clue.text: Dread making mistake on final part of test

indicators.note: on means the mistake is placed after the letter from test
final part of means the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: A student dreads a slip-up in the last section of an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of 'test' comes first, with ERROR after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Terror is extreme fear, and dread is great fear, so the nouns are near synonyms.

clue.text: Use 'Pam' or 'Ned' in a way, in attempt to impress

definitions.text: Use 'Pam' or 'Ned' in a way, in attempt to impress

indicators.note: in a way means arranged in some other fashion, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Dropping famous friends' first names into chat to impress people.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of PAM OR NED rearranged give the answer, and the whole clue also describes the act of mentioning names to impress.
explanation.definitionFit: To name-drop is to mention famous acquaintances casually so as to impress listeners.

clue.text: Otherwise acted in cunning and in sleazy way

indicators.note: in means placed inside the cunning word

parts.note: sly means cunning
or means otherwise, as in do it or else
did means acted, performed

explanation.surface: Someone behaved deviously and slyly, a shady character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Otherwise' gives OR, as in 'do it or else'; the two short words sit side by side inside the cunning word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sordidly means in a morally squalid or dishonest manner, which is a sleazy way.

clue.text: Record holder recovered after accident

parts.note: the flight recorder searched for after an air crash holds a record of the flight

explanation.walkthrough: 'Record holder' suggests a champion, but it is a device holding recorded data.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's flight data recorder is commonly called by this name and is retrieved after crashes to learn what happened.

clue.text: Outrage about queen turning up in dress

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the outrage goes round the queen

parts.note: to appal is to outrage or shock

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A queen arrives in a shocking outfit, causing outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: ER turned up becomes RE, which goes inside APPAL. ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the standard abbreviation for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is clothing, and dress is used as a general term for clothes or attire.

clue.text: States with processed fuel coming in handy

parts.note: US is the United States

indicators.note: processed means worked on and changed, so the letters of fuel are rearranged

explanation.surface: America's refined fuel proving convenient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' looks like an insertion signal, but it belongs to the definition: something useful comes in handy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something useful is of practical help, the same as something that comes in handy.

clue.text: Angle on clear fabric for hose

indicators.note: on in a down clue means placed above, so the angle word sits on top of the clear word

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line
net means clear, as in net profit after deductions

explanation.surface: An angler casts with a transparent mesh for stockings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hose' here means stockings, not a garden pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishnet is an open mesh material used for tights and stockings, which are hosiery.

clue.text: One group losing revenue, initially, as drops accumulated in freeze

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: losing means a letter is taken away from the group

parts.note: a circle is a group of people, as in a social circle

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of revenue

explanation.surface: A club losing income as things freeze over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'group' means a circle of people, as in a social circle; 'drops accumulated in freeze' is a descriptive definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An icicle forms when dripping water freezes, a hanging spike built up from frozen drops.

clue.text: Dire prospects ruined solidarity of group

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of the two words are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Bleak prospects wrecked a team's unity.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit de corps is French for the morale and fellowship shared by members of a team or unit.

clue.text: Attach to river bank

parts.note: to tie is to attach
R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: Mooring a boat to a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests a riverside, but it means a row or tier, like a bank of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row placed above another, as in a bank of seating or switches.

clue.text: Help to catch bird — booby or loon

indicators.note: to catch means to hold within, so help surrounds the bird

parts.note: aid means help
a rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: Getting help to trap a seabird or a diver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booby' and 'loon' are both birds, so they look like the bird to catch, but here they mean fools.
explanation.definitionFit: Booby and loon are both words for a silly person, and an airhead is a foolish, empty-headed one.

clue.text: Wine I had during and after singing in church

indicators.note: and after means I also appears at the end
during means placed in the course of, so I goes inside the singing

parts.note: a chant is a song sung in church services

explanation.surface: Someone had a glass of wine during and after a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: I is used twice: once 'during' CHANT, giving CHIANT, and once 'after', adding a final I.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany in Italy.

clue.text: Fish you can see in eyeglass, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: Fish visible through a monocle, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like 'strangely' but picks out the odd letters of 'eyeglass'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long snake-like fish.

clue.text: Old-fashioned print worker kind to dog

parts.note: type means kind or sort
a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A printer of the old school who is gentle with his dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kind' looks like an adjective meaning gentle, but it is the noun for a sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A typesetter arranged metal type for printing, a trade largely replaced by computers.
